root_cause.text: The hackrf driver prematurely frees its device structure (dev) via kfree() on error paths after the V4L2 device has been registered, but userspace may already hold open file descriptors, causing use-after-free and double-free when those descriptors are used or released.
root_cause.evidence: The commit description details the race: after v4l2_device_register() in hackrf_probe(), another thread opens the device, then the probe error path calls v4l2_device_unregister() and kfree(dev), while the open fd can still issue ioctl (UAF) or close (DFB). The patch replaces v4l2_device_unregister() with v4l2_device_put() and returns directly, deferring memory freeing to the release() callback.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incorrect error cleanup label in hackrf_probe to use v4l2_device_put instead of v4l2_device_unregister after video device registration failure.
intent_record.what: Changed the goto target in the error handling of hackrf_probe from err_v4l2_device_unregister to err_v4l2_device_put after a video device registration failure.
intent_record.how: This alters the cleanup routine: instead of calling v4l2_device_unregister (which removes a registered device), it now calls v4l2_device_put (which decrements the reference count). This ensures correct teardown when registration fails.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix error path in hackrf_probe to use v4l2_device_put and return immediately, preventing incorrect cleanup sequence and potential resource leaks.
intent_record.what: Changed error handling labels and function calls in hackrf_probe: renames label from `err_v4l2_device_unregister` to `err_v4l2_device_put`, replaces `v4l2_device_unregister` with `v4l2_device_put`, and inserts `return ret;` before the next label to prevent fall-through.
intent_record.how: At runtime, on an error after RX video device registration, the handler now calls `v4l2_device_put` to decrement the reference count instead of unregistering the device, and returns immediately with the error code instead of falling through to free ctrl handlers, which could cause a double free or improper cleanup.
